parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why chromium complexes are coloured.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Four different compounds can be obtained when anhydrous chromium(III) chloride reacts with water under various conditions. When samples of each compound are reacted separately with aqueous silver nitrate, different amounts of silver chloride are precipitated. The precipitation leaves the complex ions **P**, **Q**, **R** and **S** in solution.

| formula of compound | moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated per mole of complex ion | complex ion | property of complex ion |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{CrCl}_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6$ | 3 | **P** | non-polar |
| $\text{CrCl}_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5$ | 2 | **Q** | polar |
| $\text{CrCl}_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4$ | 1 | **R** | polar |
| $\text{CrCl}_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4$ | 1 | **S** | non-polar |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Draw three-dimensional diagrams for the structures of complex ions **P**, **Q**, **R** and **S**. Include the charges for each complex ion.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why complex ion **S** is non-polar.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(iii)
parts.text:
**Z** reacts with aqueous chromium(III) ions, $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, in a 3:1 ratio to form a new neutral complex.

State the coordination number and the geometry of the chromium(III) centre in the complex.

parts.stem: $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ decomposes readily on heating to form $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$, steam and an inert colourless gas.

parts.text: Deduce the oxidation numbers of chromium in $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$.
